memoryTip: Hit metal with a mallet—malleable stuff bends; minds can bend too.
correctPassage: Public opinion on the issue remains malleable, especially among younger voters.
wrongPassages: The steel beam was so malleable that not even a forge could change its shape.
She packed a malleable suitcase: one shirt and a book for a month abroad.
His malleable schedule never changed, no matter who asked for a new time.

definition: well chosen or suited to the circumstances
memoryTip: Felicity = apt happiness—a felicitous phrase is a happily perfect fit.
correctPassage: It was a felicitous choice of words that captured the mood exactly.
wrongPassages: The icy sidewalk felt felicitous after crews forgot the salt and left it glazed.
Her felicitous remark insulted every guest and emptied the room in minutes.
They called the plan felicitous because it clashed with every stated goal.

definition: extreme care and attention to detail
memoryTip: Meticulous = tiny details—meticulousness is extreme care, not speed.
correctPassage: The restorer’s meticulousness is visible in every repaired seam.
wrongPassages: His meticulousness meant skipping the checklist and guessing the measurements.
She showed meticulousness by tossing the parts in a box and walking away.
The drawer of meticulousness held one key that opened nothing in the building.

memoryTip: In + vigor: put vigor in—energize, wake up, strengthen.
correctPassage: A change of leadership can invigorate an organization that has grown stagnant.
wrongPassages: The long meeting seemed to invigorate everyone into yawning at their desks.
They hoped to invigorate the team by cancelling training and cutting coffee.
She tried to invigorate the garden by withholding water for three dry weeks.

memoryTip: Priest-clean pure—pristine means untouched, unspoiled original condition.
correctPassage: Hikers are asked to leave the trail as pristine as they found it.
wrongPassages: The dump looked pristine after weeks of litter and oil stains along the fence.
His pristine desk was buried under empty cups, sticky notes, and broken pens.
They sold the car as pristine despite the cracked windshield and missing bumper.

memoryTip: De-rogate: take rank away—derogate means diminish or speak down of.
correctPassage: Nothing in the agreement should derogate from existing labor rights.
wrongPassages: The award was meant to derogate her years of careful, widely praised research.
They hoped to derogate the mold by turning up the heat without fixing the leak.
Supporters stood to derogate the hero with a standing ovation and flowers.

memoryTip: Venus-level reverence—venerate means treat as sacred or deeply respect.
correctPassage: Many still venerate the founders while questioning later policy choices.
wrongPassages: The crowd gathered to venerate the traitor by booing him off the stage.
She hoped the gift would venerate the insult; it only reminded everyone of it.
Critics venerate a book when they call it careless, dull, and forgettable.

memoryTip: Light heart—cheerful, playful, not heavy or grim.
correctPassage: A light-hearted tone made the difficult subject easier to discuss.
wrongPassages: The funeral oration was light-hearted only if solemn and slow counts as light.
Her light-hearted lawsuit demanded years of damages for a broken mug.
The light-hearted safety chapter listed only the most severe injury protocols.

definition: cause to happen suddenly; acting rashly
memoryTip: Like rain precipitating—things fall fast; a precipitate act is rash.
correctPassage: A sudden price spike can precipitate panic selling.
wrongPassages: The board’s precipitate delay of five years showed careful, unhurried study.
They hoped to precipitate calm by spreading the decision over many quiet months.
A precipitate plan is one that waits for every risk to vanish before starting.

memoryTip: Scrutiny = close look—scrutinize means study every detail carefully.
correctPassage: Peer reviewers will scrutinize every claim before the paper is accepted.
wrongPassages: Editors scrutinize submissions by reading only the title and never opening the file.
She scrutinized the horizon for half a second and declared nothing of interest.
To scrutinize the budget, the board shredded it unread and approved a replacement.
